title: Eighth Word The Unfortunate Brothers Suspicion And Painful State

questions.question: What dangerous place does the man enter after running from the beast?
questions.answer: He jumps into a deep dry well.

questions.question: What keeps him from falling all the way down?
questions.answer: He grabs onto a tree growing from the side of the well.

questions.question: What are the two animals doing to the tree?
questions.answer: They are chewing through its two roots.

questions.question: What does the man see at the top of the well?
questions.answer: A lion waiting above him.

questions.question: What does he see below him in the well?
questions.answer: A terrifying dragon rising toward him.

questions.question: What else on the sides of the well makes his situation worse?
questions.answer: Harmful stinging creatures are gathered around him.

questions.question: Why is the tree unusual?
questions.answer: It carries many different kinds of fruit even though it is one tree.

questions.question: What does the passage say the man fails to understand about all these events?
questions.answer: He does not realize they are meaningful and under the control of a powerful being.

questions.question: How do his heart, spirit, and mind react inwardly to his condition?
questions.answer: They are in deep pain and distress.

questions.question: How does his lower self respond instead?
questions.answer: It acts like everything is fine and distracts him with the fruit.

questions.question: What poor choice does he make while hanging in danger?
questions.answer: He starts eating from the tree.

questions.question: What is important about some of the fruit he eats?
questions.answer: Some of it is harmful and poisonous.

questions.question: What lesson is connected to the sacred hadith mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: A person is dealt with according to how he thinks of Allah.

questions.question: How does the man view what is happening to him?
questions.answer: He thinks it is all normal and exactly what it seems to be.

questions.question: What result does this misunderstanding bring him?
questions.answer: He remains stuck in suffering without rescue or relief.

questions.question: Why does the narrator leave this man at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: To return and reflect on the condition of the other brother.

questions.question: In what kind of landscape does the man find himself before the attack?
questions.answer: He is in a lonely and empty wilderness.

questions.question: What first causes him to panic and run?
questions.answer: He hears a frightening sound and sees a lion coming at him.

questions.question: About how far down does he fall before stopping?
questions.answer: He stops around halfway down the well.

questions.question: What detail about the well shows how serious his danger is?
questions.answer: It is very deep and has threats above, below, and around him.

questions.question: How does the passage show that appearances can be misleading?
questions.answer: The tree looks inviting, but some of its fruit is actually harmful.

questions.question: What is the man’s main intellectual mistake?
questions.answer: He treats an extraordinary situation as if it were ordinary and meaningless.

questions.question: What spiritual mistake does his lower self make?
questions.answer: It ignores inner warnings and chooses temporary pleasure instead of understanding.

questions.question: How is there a conflict inside the man?
questions.answer: His inner being is distressed, but his lower self covers that pain with false comfort.

questions.question: Why is his eating of the fruit more than just a physical action?
questions.answer: It shows moral carelessness and being deceived by immediate desire.

questions.question: What does the hadith add to the meaning of the story at this point?
questions.answer: It shows that a person’s attitude toward Allah affects how his condition unfolds.

questions.question: What happens because he insists on seeing the situation wrongly?
questions.answer: His suffering continues without escape, death, or true life.

questions.question: What mood does the passage create by the end of this scene?
questions.answer: A mood of trapped misery, fear, and hopelessness.

questions.question: List the main threats surrounding the man in the well.
questions.answer: A lion above, a dragon below, poisonous creatures on the sides, and rats cutting through the roots.

questions.question: What object in the well gives him temporary support?
questions.answer: A tree growing from the wall of the well.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast the man’s inner reality with his outward behavior?
questions.answer: Inside he is in anguish, but outwardly he acts as if he can enjoy himself.

questions.question: What shows that the scene is not being presented as random?
questions.answer: The passage says there are hidden meanings and a powerful director behind it.

questions.question: What does the man fail to notice about the strange creatures and events?
questions.answer: He fails to see that they carry secrets and are not accidental.

questions.question: Why is the fig tree especially striking in this scene?
questions.answer: It bears many kinds of fruit that would not normally come from one tree.

questions.question: What does his lower self choose to do instead of reflecting?
questions.answer: It shuts out the cries of his inner being and goes after pleasure.

questions.question: How does self-deception appear in the passage?
questions.answer: He convinces himself that his terrible condition is nothing serious.

questions.question: What warning can a student take from the poisonous fruit?
questions.answer: Something attractive can still be spiritually or morally harmful.

questions.question: According to the passage, what connection exists between a servant’s view of Allah and his experience?
questions.answer: His experience matches the way he approaches and expects from Allah.

questions.question: What three-part description best fits the man’s final condition?
questions.answer: He is trapped, tormented, and without relief.

questions.question: What does the statement that he neither dies nor lives suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests a state of ongoing suffering with no peace.

questions.question: Why is foolishness emphasized so strongly in this passage?
questions.answer: Because his suffering is increased by his failure to think and understand correctly.

questions.question: What is the immediate purpose of ending the scene with this man still suffering?
questions.answer: It prepares the reader to compare him with the other brother.

questions.question: How does the man try to escape the lion?
questions.answer: He runs away and throws himself into a deep dry well.

questions.question: What stops his fall in the middle of the well?
questions.answer: He catches hold of a tree growing from the wall.

questions.question: What are the colors of the two rats, and what are they doing?
questions.answer: One is white and one is black, and they are gnawing at the roots.

questions.question: How close does the dragon come to him?
questions.answer: It raises its head near his foot.

questions.question: What kind of creatures are around the walls of the well?
questions.answer: Poisonous and stinging vermin.

questions.question: What surprising feature does the fig tree have?
questions.answer: It carries many different kinds of fruit.

questions.question: What should the man have understood about this strange scene?
questions.answer: He should have understood that it points to hidden meanings and wise control.

questions.question: What keeps him from reaching that understanding?
questions.answer: His thoughtlessness and foolishness.

questions.question: How do his heart and spirit react differently from his lower self?
questions.answer: They grieve deeply, while his lower self pretends there is no real problem.

questions.question: In what way does the lower self silence the truth about his condition?
questions.answer: It ignores the inner cries and turns to enjoyment.

questions.question: Why is eating the fruit a bad response in this moment?
questions.answer: Because he chases pleasure while surrounded by danger and ignores the reality of his state.

questions.question: What does the sacred hadith teach in this passage?
questions.answer: A servant’s expectation and view of Allah matter greatly.

questions.question: How does the man misread reality at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: He accepts the surface appearance as the whole truth.

questions.question: What is the outcome of that misreading?
questions.answer: He remains in continuous misery, without rescue through life or death.

questions.question: What sequence of events leads the man into the well?
questions.answer: A lion appears, he runs in fear, and then he jumps into the dry well.

questions.question: What position is he left in after falling?
questions.answer: He is hanging halfway down, holding onto a tree.

questions.question: What threats come from above, below, and beside him?
questions.answer: A lion is above, a dragon is below, and poisonous creatures are around the walls.

questions.question: What danger affects the very thing he is depending on for support?
questions.answer: Two rats are wearing away the roots of the tree.

questions.question: Why would the fruit tree make a thoughtful person stop and reflect?
questions.answer: Because one tree producing many kinds of fruit is extraordinary.

questions.question: What does the passage say the man does not understand about chance?
questions.answer: He does not realize these events are not random.

questions.question: Who is implied to be behind the strange events?
questions.answer: A powerful being directing them.

questions.question: What signs within the man show that he knows, deep down, that his state is terrible?
questions.answer: His heart, spirit, and mind are inwardly crying out in distress.

questions.question: How does the lower self mislead him?
questions.answer: It makes the danger seem unimportant and pushes him toward temporary enjoyment.

questions.question: What does his behavior teach about the danger of heedlessness?
questions.answer: A heedless person may ignore warnings and choose what harms him.

questions.question: Why is the fruit not a true solution to his problem?
questions.answer: It gives brief distraction but does nothing to save him, and some of it is harmful.

questions.question: How does the hadith deepen the moral lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that one’s spiritual outlook affects how one meets hardship.

questions.question: What is meant by saying he is treated in line with his understanding?
questions.answer: Since he insists on a blind and shallow view, he remains under the consequences of that view.

questions.question: How would you describe the man’s final state in one sentence?
questions.answer: He is suspended in ongoing torment because he fails to understand and respond rightly.

questions.question: What image begins the main crisis of the passage?
questions.answer: A lion suddenly comes out and threatens the man.

questions.question: Why does the man jump into the well?
questions.answer: He is trying to escape the lion.

questions.question: What does he find in the middle of the well that delays his fall?
questions.answer: A tree he can hold onto.

questions.question: What is happening to the tree’s roots?
questions.answer: A white rat and a black rat are chewing through them.

questions.question: What makes the dragon especially terrifying?
questions.answer: It rises from below with a huge mouth and comes very near him.

questions.question: Besides the lion and dragon, what other source of danger surrounds him?
questions.answer: Poisonous stinging creatures cover the walls nearby.

questions.question: What makes the tree different from a normal fig tree?
questions.answer: It bears many kinds of fruit instead of only one.

questions.question: What truth about the situation does the man fail to recognize?
questions.answer: He fails to see that the scene holds hidden wisdom and is under deliberate control.

questions.question: What part of him still senses the seriousness of the situation?
questions.answer: His heart, spirit, and mind sense it deeply.

questions.question: What does his lower self do with those inner warnings?
questions.answer: It ignores them and turns toward pleasure.

questions.question: How is the man’s foolishness shown in a practical way?
questions.answer: He starts eating fruit while trapped in extreme danger.

questions.question: Why is that choice even worse than it first appears?
questions.answer: Because some of the fruit is poisonous as well as distracting.

questions.question: What main idea does the hadith communicate here?
questions.answer: A servant’s opinion and expectation of Allah are spiritually significant.

questions.question: What mistaken conclusion does the man reach about what he sees?
questions.answer: He thinks the outward appearance is the full reality.

questions.question: What final condition does this lead to?
questions.answer: He remains in a state of painful misery, unable to escape.

questions.question: What is the passage preparing the reader to do next by ending this way?
questions.answer: It is preparing the reader to compare this man with the other brother.
